notes_for_editor: Date of the radio-emergency item (4 September) is from the 1923 Bulletin volume, p. 51 of 57; the year of the event is assumed 1923 from the volume. The efficiency-flag table is OCR'd in scrambled columns; Tree Point/J. C. Johnson was matched by position and by the index entry (no flag-district shown). The 1936 plane story's cutter name is OCR-garbled (looks like Cyane) so the story says only 'a Coast Guard cutter'. USLHS prints La Bryn as 1000-1000; LighthouseFriends 1904-1908. Source 4 (1918 report) and 5 (1922 services) are in the bound 1915-1922 Commissioner volume; page numbers are the printed pages from corpus.py. Optic chronology conflicts: NRHP says 4th-order occulting by 1910-1918, LHF 1913-1918 revolving, 1919 Bulletin says oil to acetylene fixed to flashing. Record's 1905 first-lit not supported. Post-1960 Coast Guard names appear in the roster only as USLHS prints them; the story names none of them. Tower height in record (20.1 m) not checked. NRHP county named 'Prince of Wales-Outer Ketchikan Census Area' (record: Prince of Wales-Hyder Borough). Newspaper search (Chronicling America) was started but returned nothing in time. Fern is named in the Bulletin text only through OCR damage ('FerlL', 'l"ern'); the story drops 'tender' and uses the name as the OCR gives it (the 1916 Commissioner report lists a tender Fern in the same district). The NRHP listing year 2004 rests on the NPS record's publication date 10/27/2004 (source 13); the nomination text itself gives no listing date. The 1918-1923 index shows Tree Point efficiency flag at pages 22 and 275: the story uses only the 1923 volume list.
